subject: Newcastle auth anomaly notification and IR evidence handoff
messages:
From: Alex Green <alex.green@newcastle-pay.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: security@newcastle-pay.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Newcastle — potential auth anomaly, initial notification

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Quick heads up from our side: we detected a short-lived spike of authentication events tied to a single API key for three merchant accounts overnight (approx. 02:07–02:24 UTC). We're treating this as a potential token reuse / misconfiguration event. No confirmed customer data exfiltration at this time, but we need to validate.

Can Redwood share the following as soon as practical so our SOC team can triage?
- Any server-side logs showing token validation failures / sudden reuse across sessions
- The IRP you use for cloud-hosted model endpoints and expected preservation window for telemetry
- A contact for any expedited requests (phone + PGP)

We're preparing a formal request but wanted to notify you immediately. We're happy to coordinate via a screened channel — prefer encrypted attachment for any logs.

Thanks,
Alex Green
Head of Information Security
Newcastle Payments
alex.green@newcastle-pay.com
+1 (415) 555-0133

Alex — thank you for the alert and for the context. We're treating this as high priority.

> Quick heads up from our side: we detected a short-lived spike of authentication events tied to a single API key for three merchant accounts overnight ...

2) Neha (security ops) will coordinate a secure artifact transfer and redaction plan.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@newcastle-pay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Newcastle — potential auth anomaly, initial notification — postmortem and artifacts

Alex / team — closing the loop from Redwood's side.

Summary: we reviewed telemetry for 02:00–03:30 UTC and confirmed repeated token reuse originating from a mis-rotated service token deployed in one of our edge routers. The router configuration pushed an older token that had been decommissioned at the backend but remained accepted by a caching layer. No authenticated data export was observed; all access attempts were blocked after our automated mitigation at 02:28 UTC.

Actions taken (high level):
- 02:30 UTC: rotated and revoked the impacted token; invalidated router cache entries
- 03:05 UTC: pushed a hotfix to the router config deploy pipeline to prevent token reintroduction
- 04:10 UTC: validated no subsequent auth anomalies in the following 24 hrs
- Ongoing: 7‑day telemetry retention snapshot saved to our IR archive for your compliance review

Attached: postmortem_summary.pdf (root cause, timeline, remediation), newcastle_ir_artifacts_v1.zip (redacted logs + manifest), audit_log_excerpt.csv

Next steps we recommend for Newcastle:
- Validate merchant-side token rotation schedules and ensure tokens are not re-used across environments
- Add a short TTL on router cache entries that accept tokens from legacy pipelines
- If you want, we can schedule a 30‑minute technical walk-through this week to go over the artifacts and queries we ran.

If this suffices for your SOC/SIG intake, indicate and we'll publish the evidence bundle to the Drive link (shared above) and provide a signed evidence receipt.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
